A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same All-atom Diffusion Transformer work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–E are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated content.

before.justification: v1 reports original molecule, crystal, and metal-organic framework generation results, alongside scaling experiments, ablations, and latent-space analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds GEOM-DRUGS generation results and inference-time measurements.

M1.justification: The unified representation, VAE, reconstruction objectives, DiT, conditioning, and sampling algorithms remain unchanged. Applying ADiT to GEOM-DRUGS does not introduce a documented method modification.

E1.justification: v2 adds GEOM-DRUGS, described as 430,000 organic molecules with up to 180 atoms. This substantially extends molecular coverage beyond small QM9 molecules. MP20 and QMOF coverage is retained; the MOF experiment moves to Appendix C.

E2.justification: The new GEOM-DRUGS comparison introduces EQGAT-diff and SemlaFlow, neither evaluated as a comparator in v1. SemlaFlow also provides a new efficiency comparator. Table 3 attributes their PoseBusters results to Buttenschoen et al. (2025); existing comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The added GEOM-DRUGS experiment follows Vignac et al. (2023), reports an aggregate PoseBusters-valid metric, and measures generation time for 10,000 molecules on one A100. These are additional evaluation settings; the existing QM9, MP20, and MOF protocols are retained.

E4.justification: Table 3 adds an efficiency-scaling analysis varying integration steps and ADiT model size against SemlaFlow on larger molecules. Existing architecture and regularization ablations, sampling sensitivity studies, crystal-distribution analyses, and PCA visualizations are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report three-seed sensitivity analyses with 95% confidence intervals in Figure 6. v2 retains that reporting and introduces no additional repeated-run or uncertainty reporting for GEOM-DRUGS.

E6.justification: Table 3 adds substantial GEOM-DRUGS quality and timing results. ADiT reports 95.3% validity versus SemlaFlow's 93.9%, but 85.3% overall PoseBusters validity versus 87.5%. These are new benchmark findings, not improvements over v1 under matched settings. Existing benchmark and ablation values are retained.

T1.justification: The mathematical representation, reconstruction losses, and flow-matching formulation in equations (1)–(12) are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract moderates performance from 'exceeding' specialized models to being 'on par,' while the introduction adds an explicit competitive-performance claim for larger GEOM-DRUGS molecules. The central unified-generation, transfer-learning, and scalability contributions remain intact.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the GEOM-DRUGS results as supporting competitive generation without explicit bond prediction or strong molecular inductive biases. Section 5 changes the stated demonstrated scale from tens to hundreds of atoms, while retaining limitations concerning thousand-atom systems and conditional generation.

D1.justification: v2 identifies A100 hardware for the new timing experiment and provides sources for its GEOM-DRUGS setup and borrowed baseline PoseBusters results. Existing implementation details, hyperparameters, and code-access information remain unchanged; benchmark-specific training documentation remains brief.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting GEOM-DRUGS, its protocol, and the new comparators. Appendix A also adds language-model generation and non-equivariant molecular-generation references. These are localized expansions of related work rather than a fundamental repositioning.

P1.justification: The MOF subsection moves from the main results to Appendix C, and GEOM-DRUGS takes its place in the main narrative. Abstract, discussion, related-work, and publication-header edits are localized; most prose and the overall organization remain stable.

P2.justification: v2 adds the GEOM-DRUGS table and adjacent runtime plot, relocates the original MOF Table 3 as Appendix Table 4, and adjusts subsequent table numbering. Figure 2's caption is corrected to describe runtime rather than validity; existing figures and tables are otherwise largely retained.

improvement.justification: GEOM-DRUGS provides useful direct evidence for ADiT's applicability to larger molecules and its efficiency against a stronger relevant comparator, while the original evidence is preserved. The corrected Figure 2 caption also improves clarity. The gain is bounded by brief experimental documentation and mixed outcomes: ADiT's overall PoseBusters validity remains below SemlaFlow's despite broad competitive-performance wording.
